title: Screening Edited iPSC Clones
author: Celeste M M. Karch

steps_raw.instruction: Genomic Editing: iPSC

Split cells into 3 wells of a 6 well plate 48 hours prior to nucleofection (plan for cells to be confluent in 48 hours). You will need 3 million cells per nucleofection, so 3-6 confluent wells should be sufficient
Split 1 well of 6 well plate into 3 wells of a 6 well plate
Coat 6 well plate with 1mL Matrigel (supplemented with RGD fragment) for 1 hour
Wash with 1-2mL PBS per well
Add 1mL accutase per well
Incubate at 37*C for 5-10 minutes to achieve single cells
Collect cells in 5mL DMEM/F12 and transfer to a 15mL conical tube
Spin at 750-800 rpm for 3 minutes
Resuspend cells in mTesR1 (2mL per well) supplemented with 1uM Rock Inhibitor
Plate 2mL of cells per well on a Matrigel (supplemented with RGD fragment) coated plate
Change media daily with mTesR1
Coat plate for nucleofection (2-3 wells) with Matrigel supplemented with RGD for 1 hour
Just prior to splitting cells for nucleofection, equilibrate Matrigel/RGD coated plate with 3-5mL/well DMEM/F12+10% FBS supplemented with 10uM Rock Inhibitor
Aliquot DNA into 1.7mL tubes using the below table
Split cells for nucleofection
Wash with 1-2mL PBS per well
Add 1mL accutase per well
Incubate at 37*C for 5-10 minutes (check at 5 minutes) to achieve single cells
Collect cells in 5mL PBS and transfer to 15mL conical tube
Spin at 750-800 rpm for 3 minutes
Resuspend cell pellet in 3mL PBS in 15mL conical
Pipette 10uL into cell counter
Using all four corners of the countess slide, calculate the average number of cells
Multiple the average by 10,000 (10^4)
Multiple product from step “9b” by 3 to get the total number of cells
_______ average number of cells x 10,000 x 3 = total number of cells
Calculate 3 million cells
Take total number of cells calculated in step “9c” and divide by 3 million
Take answer from step 10a and divide by 3 to get the volume of cells necessary for nucleofection
Transfer the desired volume of cells to micro centrifuge tube
Centrifuge cells at 90xg for 5 minutes
Make reaction mix from Lonza Kit: P3 Primary Cell 4D (V4XP-3024) – Total of 100ul per nucleofection
Combine Reaction Mix from step 14 (100ul) with previously aliquoted DNA from step 5
Mix Reaction Mix + DNA with cell pellet by pipetting up and down with p200 pipette (try to pipette minimal times, pipette only until mixed)
Transfer 100ul to cuvette
Nucleofect with Lonza program CA-137 in P3 solution
Add small amount of media to cuvette via dropper in order to obtain all the cells from the cuvette
Transfer cells/DNA solution to appropriately pre-coated well containing 2mLs of DMEM/F12+10% FBS+10uM Rock Inhibitor
Incubate at 37*C overnight
Continue culturing the iPSC in 1 well of a 6 well plate for 5-7 days post nucleofection, changing mTesR1 daily
24 hours post nucleofection – add mTesR1 with 5uM Rock Inhibitor
48 hours post nucleofection – add mTesR1 with 2.5uM Rock Inhibitor
72 hours post nucleofection – add mTesR1 with 1uM Rock Inhibitor
Continue culturing in mTesR1 until confluent
Coat 3 wells of a 6 well plate with 1mL Matrigel (supplemented with RGD fragment)
Wash with 1-2mL PBS per well
Add 1mL Accutase per well
Incubate at 37*C for 10 minutes to achieve single cells
Collect cells in 5mL DMEM/F12 and transfer to 15mL conical tube
Spin at 750-800rpm for 3 minutes
Resuspend cells in mTesR1 supplemented with 5uM Rock Inhibitor
Plate several dilutions of cells over the three wells (typically 25ul, 50ul and 75ul in 2mLs of mTesR1)
Freeze down the remaining cells by adding an equal volume of 2x iPSC Freezing Media (20% DMSO in FBS)
Incubate at 37*C overnight
Change mTesR1 the following day

Note: It takes approximately 1 week for single cell iPSC to proliferate into small, pickable clones. In picking clones, find the balance between large enough in size that the cells will survive the picking but not so large that they are no longer isolated. If necessary, pick across several days, giving the smaller clones more time to grow.
Coat 96 well plate with 50ul Matrigel per well. Incubate at 37*C for one hour
Prior to picking, aspirate Matrigel. Replace with 50ul mTesR1 + 10uM Rock Inhibitor
Using p20, pick individual clones and place into unique wells. Use a new tip with each clone
Incubate at 37*C overnight
Change media daily (150ul mTesR1)
Screening Edited iPSC Clones
Expanding and gDNA Extraction from iPSC Clones

Note: It takes approximately 1 week for iPSC picked into 96 well plates to be sufficiently confluent for freezing and screening. For screening purposes, a fraction of the cells picked into one well of a 96 well plate will be saved for DNA Extraction and the remaining will be kept in culture or frozen down.
Splitting 96 Well Plates for gDNA Extraction and Continuing Culture
Note: split cells upon reaching maximum 80% confluence and minimum 40%
Coat 96 well plate with 50uL Matrigel per well
Incubate at 37C for one hour
Prepare plate for expansion by aspirating Matrigel from plate
Add 50uL mTesR1 + 10uM Rock Inhibitor to appropriate wells
Aspirate media from original plate
Wash with 200uL PBS and aspirate
Add 25uL of 0.05% Trypsin
Incubate at 37C for 5 minutes
Tap to lift cells from plate
Check under microscope to ensure that cells have detached from plate
Add 50uL FBS and tap to mix
Transfer 50uL to 96 well PCR plate, while maintaining the location of each sample (this plate will be used for gDNA extraction)
Transfer remaining cells (~30uL) to 96 well plate containing mTesR1
After 24 hours, complete daily media changes with mTesR1
Splitting 96 Well Plates for gDNA Extraction and Freezing Down
Note: split cells upon reaching maximum 80% confluence and minimum 40%
Aspirate media from original plate
Wash with 200uL PBS and aspirate
Add 25uL of 0.05% Trypsin
Incubate at 37C for 5 minutes
Tap to lift cells from plate
Check under microscope to ensure that cells have detached from plate
Add 45uL mTesR1 to plate and tap to mix
Transfer 15uL to a 96 well PCR plate, while maintaining the location of each sample (this plate will be used for gDNA extraction)
Add 50uL of 2X Freezing Media (20% DMSO in FBS) to cell plate and tap to mix
Wrap plate in parafilm. Add tape over parafilm. Label the plate on the outside of the tape
Place plate in Styrofoam box. Fill any open areas with diapers, paper towels, or kimwipes. Cover box and make sure that lid is closed completely.
Store in -80C for up to 4 months
iPSC gDNA Extraction: For Screening Edited Clones
Spin 96 well PCR plate at 3800 rpm for 30 minutes at 4C
Pipet off supernatant
If worried about removing cells, transfer supernatant with multichannel pipet into new PCR plates and store at -20C until DNA extraction is complete
To cell pellet (often not visible), add 50uL QuickExtract DNA Solution (Epicentre Technologies QE09050)
Vortex plate for 15 seconds
Incubate plate in thermocycler at 65C for 6 minutes
Vortex plate for 15 seconds
Incubate plate in thermocycler at 98C for 2 minutes
Place plate in -20C for storage, until ready to use for further screening experiments
iPSC PCR: For Screening Edited Clones
Using the extracted gDNA, set up the following PCR and run using the following conditions.
Each cell line/mutation will require its own unique set of primers. Ensure that you have the appropriate primers for the cell line/mutation before setting up the PCR
Note: Design primers to amplify approximately a 300-400bp region for best results
This is the set up for 50uL reaction
After PCR has been set up, run in thermocycler using the following conditions
After PCR has been run in thermocycler, it is best to run the sample on a 2% gel to confirm the presence of PCR product.
To make the gel, combine an appropriate amount of Agarose, TBE and Ethidium Bromide using the following guidelines
The 2% gel will be cast in one of the following ways
3.75 uL of Ethidium Bromide
7.5 uL of Ethidium Bromide
Combine Agarose and TBE in an appropriately sized flask and microwave until Agarose is completely dissolved. Swirl intermittently during heating
Once completely dissolved add appropriate amount of Ethidium Bromide to flask and swirl until dispersed evenly
Pour gel from flask into casting tray (be sure to add appropriate amount of combs to casting tray)
Let sit for 30-40 minutes, or until firm
Place gel cast into the gel rig apparatus
Note: Be sure to include positive and negative controls when possible
Place lid on gel rig apparatus
Run gel at 150 volts for 90 minutes (checking at 60 minutes to ensure samples have not run too far or off the gel)
Turn off gel rig apparatus and remove cast
Blot off excess TBE from cast
Take to Syngene Imager (located between Holtzman/Cruchaga/Fagan labs)
Place gel cast into the imager, trying to center it as much as possible
Log in using PSYCH username and password
Open Syngene Software and set appropriate parameters to obtain an adequate image
Take multiple images and save
iPSC Restriction Digest: For Screening Edited Clones
Note: If no cut sites exist for mutation/correction in question, T7 assay should be performed instead
After confirming the presence of the appropriate sized PCR product, you can move on to performing a restriction digest
Identify the appropriate enzyme for the cell line/mutation in question
A mutation or correction may either introduce or destroy a cut site
Introducing a new cut site tends to give better results than destroying a cut site
Destroying a cut site tends to result in a high rate of false positives
Prepare the following reagents in a strip cap tube with the previously identified enzyme
Run in Thermocylcer at the appropriate incubation temperature for the enzyme being used (e.g. 37C, 42C, 25C, etc.)
Incubate at appropriate temperature for 2-3 hours
After Restriction Digest has been run in thermocycler, it is best to run the sample on a 2% gel to confirm the presence of appropriate product.
To make the gel, combine an appropriate amount of Agarose, TBE and Ethidium Bromide using the following guidelines
The 2% gel will be cast in one of the following ways
3.75 uL of Ethidium Bromide
7.5 uL of Ethidium Bromide
Combine Agarose and TBE in an appropriately sized flask and microwave until Agarose is completely dissolved. Swirl intermittently during heating
Once completely dissolved add appropriate amount of Ethidium Bromide to flask and swirl until dispersed evenly
Pour gel from flask into casting tray (be sure to add appropriate amount of combs to casting tray)
Let sit for 30-40 minutes, or until firm
Place gel cast into the gel rig apparatus
Place lid on gel rig apparatus
Run gel at 150 volts for 90 minutes (checking at 60 minutes to ensure samples have not run too far or off the gel)
Turn off gel rig apparatus and remove cast
Blot off excess TBE from cast
Take to Syngene Imager (located between Holtzman/Cruchaga/Fagan labs)
Place gel cast into the imager, trying to center it as much as possible
Log in using PSYCH username and password
Open Syngene Software and set appropriate parameters to obtain an adequate image
Take multiple images and save
Analyze gel images and select potentially edited clones based on banding patterns.
After identifying clones with the appropriate banding pattern, clone gDNA should be sequenced in order to confirm genotype. To do this, set up a sequencing reaction as outlined below.
Perform PCR on gDNA using the following TouchDown Protocol (50μL reaction)
Set up PCR on ice, add reagents in desired order (however it is best to add the polymerase and gDNA last)
After product has been run in the thermocycler –
Run 15μL of each sample on a 2% gel to determine presence of PCR product
Run product on gel at 150V for 90 minutes
After confirming the presence of PCR product, move on to sequencing reaction protocol below
Use Eurofins prelabeled tubes. Send out a Forward and a Reverse for each sample (1 tube get a forward primer, another tube gets a reverse primer, they do not go in the same tube together)
Be sure to document the barcode number and tube position before sending off
Determine which clones to expand based on screening
Coat 24 well plate with 250-300ul Matrigel per well (1 well per well from 96 well).
Incubate at 37C for one hour
Remove Styrofoam box from -80C and remove plate
Place plate in 37C incubator for 15-20 minutes to thaw.
Check on plate after 15 minutes to avoid over-thawing
To each well add 10uM Rocki and mTesR1
Remove desired cells from appropriate wells and transfer to 1.7mL tube. Spin off freezing media. Plate cells in fresh plate
Remove desired cells from appropriate wells and transfer to 1.7mL tube. Dilute 1:5 (final volume of 500uL) in mTesR1 and plate in 24 well plate
Incubate at 37C overnight
Determine which clones to expand based on screening
Coat the 24 well plate with 250-300μL of Matrigel (1 well per well from 96 well) for 1 hour
Aspirate media from 96 well plate
Wash with 200-500μL PBS and aspirate
Add 25μL of 0.05% trypsin and incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes
During incubation, prepare Matrigel-coated plate by adding 400μL of mTesR1 + 10μM Rock Inhibitor to each well
Tap to lift cells from 96 well plate
75μL of Complete Media (DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS) and tap to mix the 96 well plate
Transfer cells to plate containing mTesR1 + Rock Inhibitor
Incubate overnight at 37°C
Gently wash cells with 1x PBS
Use 2-3mL per well in 6 well plate
Add Accutase (Gibbco A11105-01) directly to the cells and incubate at 37°C for 3-4 minutes
6 well plate, add 0.75-1mL per well
Tap dish to aid in dislocation of cells
Add DMEM/F12 directly to cells
6 well plate, add 2-4mL per well
If cells remain attached, use a cell scraper to gently dislodge cells (apply gentle pressure and use 1-2 passes to remove cells)
Collect cells in conical tube (15mL/50mL depending on volume)
Add 2-5mL DMEM/F12 to dish to remove all cells from the dish and add to conical tube
Centrifuge cells at 750rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature
Carefully aspirate supernatant
To avoid aspirating cell pellet, it is OK to leave a small amount of media (0.5-1mL)
Resuspend cell pellet with mTesR1 (No Rock Inhibitor)
Use volume appropriate for freezing
Assume 1mL per cryovial total and add ½ total volume of mTesR1
Pipet cells 1-2 times only to preserve cell clumps
Example: to freeze 10 tubes, you will need 10mL total and will add 5mL mTesR1 to cell pellet (and 5mL of 2x Freezing Media below)
Add an equal volume of cold 2x Freezing Media (20% DMSO, FBS). Pipet cells 1 time only to preserve cell clumps
Transfer cell suspension to pre-labeled cryovials (1mL per cryovial)
Ensure that cryovials are labeled with the following
Freeze vials at -80°C in foam racks for 48-72 hours
Transfer vials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage
Note: Starting Material: 1 confluent 6 well plate
Note: Use 2 wells to characterize the iPSC and 4 wells for freezing the iPSC
Coat T25 flask, chamber slide and plates with Matrigel 1 hour prior to passaging
Wash with 1mL PBS per well and aspirate
Add 1mL Accutase per well of 6 well plate
Incubate in 37°C for 3-4 minutes
Collect cells from 2 wells with 3mL DMEM/F12 per well and transfer into 15mL conical A
Collect cells from 4 wells with 3mL DMEM/F12 per well and transfer into 15mL conical B
Spin cells at 750rpm for 3 minutes
Aspirate media from each tube
To 15mL conical tube A, add 2mL mTesR1 and distribute cells
Karyotype: Add 2mls of mTesR1 to T25 flask, then add 500μL cells
gDNA pellet: 500μL cells in 1.7mL tube, spin down at max speed for 15 seconds, aspirate media, store in -80°C
RNA pellet: 900μL cells in 1.7mL tube, spin down at max speed for 15 seconds, aspirate media, store in -80°C
ICC: Dilute 100μL cells in 750μL mTesR1. Plate 200μL cells per well in 4 wells of a chamber slide
To 15mL conical tube B, add 4mL mTesR1 and 4mL of 2x Freezing Media (20% DMSO, FBS)
Add 1mL cell suspension to each vial (1 well will freeze down into approximately 2 vials)
Cryovials need to be labeled with the following before freezing down
